questions.text:
A data driven machine is one that executes an instruction if the needed data is available. The physical ordering of the code listing does not dictate the course of execution. Consider the following pseudo-code:

A. Multiply E by 0.5 to get F
B. Add A and B to get E
C. Add B with 0.5 to get D
D. Add E and F to get G
E. Add A with 10.5 to get C

Assume A,B,C are already assigned values and the desired output is G. Which of the following sequence of execution is valid?
questions.solution:
Dependencies: E = A + B (instruction B) needs A, B; F = E [latex]\times[/latex] 0.5 (A) needs E; G = E + F (D) needs E and F; D = B + 0.5 (C) and C = A + 10.5 (E) need only the given values.

Order C, B, E, A, D: compute D, then E, then C, then F (after E), then G (after E and F) True. The other orders use E or F before they exist.

Answer: C, B, E, A, D

questions.text:
A processor has 16 integer registers (R0, R1,...,R15) and 64 floating point registers (F0, F1,...,F63). It uses a 2-byte instruction format. There are four categories of instructions: Type-1, Type-2, Type-3, and Type-4. Type-1 category consists of four instructions, each with 3 integer register operands (3Rs). Type-2 category consists of eight instructions, each with 2 floating point register operands (2Fs). Type-3 category consists of fourteen instructions, each with one integer register operand and one floating point register operand (1R+1F). Type-4 category consists of N instructions, each with a floating point register operand (1F).
The maximum value of N is __________.
questions.solution:
Integer register = 4 bits, FP register = 6 bits, instruction = 16 bits. Use expanding opcodes:
- Type-1 (12 operand bits): 4-bit opcode, uses 4 of 16 codes.
- Type-2 (12 bits): 4-bit opcode, uses 8 codes [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 4 left.
- Type-3 (10 bits): 6-bit opcode: 4 [latex]\times[/latex] 4 = 16 codes, uses 14 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 2 left.
- Type-4 (6 bits): 10-bit opcode: 2 [latex]\times[/latex] [latex]2^4[/latex] = 32.

Answer: 32

questions.text:
The instruction pipeline of a RISC processor has the following stages: Instruction Fetch (IF), Instruction Decode (ID), Operand Fetch (OF), Perform Operation (PO) and Writeback (WB). The IF, ID, OF and WB stages take 1 clock cycle each for every instruction. Consider a sequence of 100 instructions. In the PO stage, 40 instructions take 3 clock cycles each, 35 instructions take 2 clock cycles each, and the remaining 25 instructions take 1 clock cycle each. Assume that there are no data hazards and no control hazards.
The number of clock cycles required for completion of execution of the sequence of instructions is ______.
questions.solution:
The PO stage is the bottleneck, so the instructions flow through it back to back.
Total PO time = 40 [latex]\times[/latex] 3 + 35 [latex]\times[/latex] 2 + 25 [latex]\times[/latex] 1 = 215 cycles.

Add 3 cycles before the first PO (IF, ID, OF) and 1 after the last (WB): 3 + 215 + 1 = 219

Answer: 219

questions.text:
The size of the physical address space of a processor is [latex]2^{P}[/latex] bytes. The word length is [latex]2^{W}[/latex] bytes. The capacity of cache memory is [latex]2^{N}[/latex] Bytes. The size of each cache block is [latex]2^{M}[/latex] words. For a K-way set-associative cache memory, the length (in number of bits) of the
tag field is
questions.solution:
Address = P bits. A K-way cache of [latex]2^N[/latex] bytes has [latex]2^N/K[/latex] bytes per way, so set index + block offset = [latex]N-\log_2K[/latex] bits.

Tag = [latex]P-(N-\log_2K)=P-N+\log_2K[/latex]

Answer: [latex]P-N+\log_2K[/latex]

questions.text: A 32-bit wide main memory unit with a capacity of 1 GB is built using 256M x 4-bit DRAM chips. The number of rows of memory cells in the DRAM chip is [latex]2^{14}[/latex]. The time taken to perform one refresh operation is 50 nanoseconds. The refresh period is 2 milliseconds. The percentage (rounded to the closest integer) of the time available for performing the memory read/write operations in the main memory unit is __________.
questions.solution:
Each 256M [latex]\times[/latex] 4 chip refreshes its [latex]2^{14}[/latex] rows one at a time: [latex]2^{14}\times50[/latex] ns = 819.2 [latex]\mu[/latex]s in every 2 ms (all chips refresh in parallel).

Refresh takes 0.8192 / 2 = 40.96% of the time, leaving about 59% for reads and writes.

Answer: 59
